title: Project protocol contract and runtime foundation
supersedes: CXRG-FE-PHASE1-2026-11-18 (merged as PR #3); phase-0 contract revision

include: Pin Res, Mes, and Chat protocol definitions and versioning evidence
Define a 3-by-3 inbound/outbound protocol capability matrix and failure semantics
Draft normalized domain and local control/data-plane interface contracts
Record Desktop and Gateway lifecycle, listener, single-instance, and startup decisions
Threat model credentials, local control access, SSRF, request limits, and logs
Prepare independently reviewable acceptance criteria for later implementation stages
Correct stale README and architecture-tree statements about Desktop frontend availability
Implement runnable local configuration and encrypted secret storage
Implement loopback control API for upstreams, routes, and client keys
Implement authenticated Gateway routing with native forwarding and TextCore-1 conversion
Add runtime tests for persistence, control plane, authentication, routing, and conversion
Add local health and backup/rollback operational entrypoints
exclude: Desktop IPC integration beyond the current runtime bridge, complex tool-result chains, migrations, deployment, and release

acceptance: Owner-approved protocol identities, API versions, and scope are recorded with official references
All nine protocol directions have explicit capability and unsupported-feature behavior
Domain, control-plane, data-plane, lifecycle, and security contracts are reviewable
Architecture decisions identify unresolved items and their owners; no decision is inferred from static code
README distinguishes the runnable fixture-backed Desktop UI from unimplemented Gateway/backend runtime
Architecture tree distinguishes implemented Desktop shell from unimplemented Gateway services
Document links, JSON contract, and Git diff checks pass
Independent review findings are addressed or explicitly reported
Runtime foundation tests pass with no external provider dependency
rollback: Revert only this contract revision, runtime foundation files, planning documents, task record, and Desktop status corrections; preserve all unrelated worktree content.
